_comments: WHAT an automation rule does. PROTOTYPE vocabulary for tracker issue #31 — nothing executes
The first two are the actions Pipeline.CloseWonPolicy ALREADY implies, which is the whole reason
the overlap between that column and these tables is an open question (PHASE3-DECISIONS-QUEUE.md
Q1). They name capabilities only bizapps-contracts and bizapps-orders can perform, and sales is
standalone today — so they are listed because the policy JSON already asks for them, not because
SET_FIELD is deliberately absent. An action that writes an arbitrary column is a rules engine
with unrestricted write access to the deal, and it would let a rule bypass every guarantee the
entity server exists to enforce — the close lock, the OwnerEmployeeID stamp, the no-arithmetic
rule. That is a design decision, not an oversight, and it is queued (Q2) rather than assumed.

fields.Name: Create a contract
fields.Description: Hand the deal to bizapps-contracts as the provenance of an agreement. Exactly what CloseWonPolicy's CreateContract / ContractTypeCode keys already declare. Cannot run until contracts is installed.

fields.Name: Create an order
fields.Description: Materialize the deal's lines into bizapps-orders. CloseWonPolicy's OneTimeLinesTo / SubscriptionLinesTo / OrderState keys already say where and in what state. Cannot run until orders is installed.

fields.Name: Notify someone
fields.Description: Tell a person something happened — the deal owner, the team, a manager. The only seeded action with no cross-app dependency, so the only one a prototype engine could plausibly implement first.

fields.Name: Create a follow-up task
fields.Description: Put work on somebody's list. Has no target table in sales today — there is no Task entity here, and whether one belongs in sales or in common is the same question the Activities prototype raises (queue Q4). Listed as vocabulary, not as a capability.
